# Fix padded tensor semantics and commitment execution

Padded reshape lowering can reorder real elements, finite masks can leave a masked score dominant, and nested commitment worker pools can exhaust the stack. This change preserves the intended tensor values, enforces the supported masking range and keeps commitment execution correct under nested parallel calls.

**Topic** correctness. **Type** Correctness and resource hardening. **Base** `perf/round-2` at `cfcffb05dcc76599f4e5b3d01c6e13f5fa653e13`.

**Primary source PRs** [#292](https://github.com/ICME-Lab/jolt-atlas/pull/292), [#293](https://github.com/ICME-Lab/jolt-atlas/pull/293), [#335](https://github.com/ICME-Lab/jolt-atlas/pull/335).

## Review order

1. Correct finite masks and centered subtraction as separate, attributed changes.
2. Preserve padded reshape order and all shadow-tracing modes.
3. Remove nested commitment pool creation.
4. Review small lint and activation-test repairs separately from protocol changes.

## Existing evidence

These are recorded comparisons for individual changes. Each has its own control and workload; performance of the combined branch is unmeasured. The original PRs retain source revisions, hardware, flags and artifact links.

| Scope | Recorded control | Recorded candidate | Meaning and limits |
|---|---|---|---|
| Attention mask, scale 14 | [0, 20] + [0, -12] gives [0, 8] | Masked positions receive zero probability in the recorded corrected fixture | Correctness example from #292, not a speedup |
| One recorded Qwen prompt, last-logit cosine | 0.931922 | 0.999874 | #293; reference next token and top ten restored; not a general accuracy claim |

## Implementation and review examples

The mask regression proves and verifies an add/softmax graph. A second fixture exercises `i32::MAX - i32::MIN` centering without truncating the difference. Imported reshape fixtures now compare integer execution, ordinary shadow, isolated shadow and original-weight shadow execution, and reject a changed public output.

Antoine's centering repair from #366 is included as an attributed commit. Its PR and original base branch are preserved. The scalar equality repair stays with the native multiplication foundation, and the Boolean-coordinate opening repair stays with the tensor operators. Small lint and activation-test repairs are separate commits.

## Validation

Linux validation at `0b28a6baff0ee3bf499726c0d3e63d703f3b007b`, Rust 1.95.0, strict warnings, eight Rayon workers and the repository test profile:

- Formatting and `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets` pass.
- `cargo test --workspace --lib` passes 356 tests, with 27 existing ignored tests. This includes the complete mask/add/softmax and imported reshape regressions.
- `cargo check -p jolt-atlas-core --all-targets --features zk` still fails in the experimental ONNX dispatcher. The exact unchanged base reports 50 primary diagnostics; this head reports 41, all matching the base by message and source location. The nine removed diagnostics concern the repaired activation tests. Native BlindFold is validated in its own replacement.

Sources were authenticated file by file, workspace crates were cleared between source trees, and the base/candidate checks ran in sequence. These are local Linux results; repository CI is reported separately. No combined performance measurement is claimed.

# Reduce ordinary verifier work and compact HyperKZG proofs

Ordinary verification rebuilds public tables and selectors, repeats commitment arithmetic, and carries redundant proof encoding. Serial consumers also inherit ONNX import and parallel-runtime dependencies. This change reuses deterministic verifier work, preserves serial iterator semantics, and adds a bounded optional encoding that restores the original canonical proof bytes.

**Topic** ordinary verifier and transport. **Type** Performance, portability and decoder hardening. **Base** `review/tensor-correctness` ([#369](https://github.com/ICME-Lab/jolt-atlas/pull/369), review unit 1).

**Primary source PRs** [#294](https://github.com/ICME-Lab/jolt-atlas/pull/294), [#295](https://github.com/ICME-Lab/jolt-atlas/pull/295), [#296](https://github.com/ICME-Lab/jolt-atlas/pull/296), [#297](https://github.com/ICME-Lab/jolt-atlas/pull/297), [#298](https://github.com/ICME-Lab/jolt-atlas/pull/298), [#299](https://github.com/ICME-Lab/jolt-atlas/pull/299), [#300](https://github.com/ICME-Lab/jolt-atlas/pull/300), [#301](https://github.com/ICME-Lab/jolt-atlas/pull/301), [#302](https://github.com/ICME-Lab/jolt-atlas/pull/302), [#308](https://github.com/ICME-Lab/jolt-atlas/pull/308), [#309](https://github.com/ICME-Lab/jolt-atlas/pull/309), [#310](https://github.com/ICME-Lab/jolt-atlas/pull/310), [#311](https://github.com/ICME-Lab/jolt-atlas/pull/311), [#312](https://github.com/ICME-Lab/jolt-atlas/pull/312), [#313](https://github.com/ICME-Lab/jolt-atlas/pull/313), [#314](https://github.com/ICME-Lab/jolt-atlas/pull/314), [#315](https://github.com/ICME-Lab/jolt-atlas/pull/315).

## Review order

1. Serial build and iterator semantics, including equal-length zip checks.
2. Common polynomial evaluation and commitment arithmetic.
3. Direct reshape, slice, concat and broadcast selectors.
4. Public activation caches and optional fixed tables.
5. Compact ordinary encoding and its decoder rejection tests.

## Existing evidence

These are recorded comparisons for individual changes. Each has its own control and workload; performance of the combined branch is unmeasured. The original PRs retain source revisions, hardware, flags and artifact links.

| Scope | Recorded control | Recorded candidate | Change | Meaning and limits |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Prepared grouped-proof guest, activation cache only | 23,032,033,118 cycles | 8,109,826,681 cycles | 14,922,206,437 fewer cycles (64.79%) | #309; 64.79% fewer cycles on the same saved proof; not outer proving time |
| Ordinary Qwen proof encoding | 5,188,295 bytes | 2,941,543 bytes | 2,246,752 fewer bytes (43.30%) | #315; 43.30% smaller, exact canonical recovery |
| Optional fixed tables, control already uses activation cache | 8,109,826,681 cycles | 7,112,443,367 cycles | 997,383,314 fewer cycles (12.30%) | #311; same saved proof; binary-size tradeoff below |
| Optional guest binary with fixed tables | 7,407,016 bytes | 8,981,352 bytes | 1,574,336 more bytes (21.25%) | #311 tradeoff; 1,574,336 more bytes |

## Implementation and review examples

The serial facade checks both lengths before constructing `zip_eq`, including empty/nonempty mismatches. Equal-length pairs and immediate rejection run under both feature configurations. ONNX-dependent fixtures are gated at their callers. Independent tensor, polynomial and proof tests remain available without ONNX import. Helpers added by round two also use the facade.

The optional affine multiscalar multiplication (MSM) and fixed tables retain explicit feature flags. The default HyperKZG combination uses the shared MSM implementation. The compact decoder checks bounds and reconstructs the canonical proof bytes.

## Measurement conditions

The activation-cache and optional fixed-table results use the same saved Qwen proof, Rust 1.95, release overflow checks and inline Blake2. The fixed-table control already includes the activation cache; its validation guest is separate from the measured optimized guest. The #309 comparison isolates caching; #311 then isolates embedded tables. Both measure executed guest cycles. [Pinned source and receipts](https://github.com/ICME-Lab/zkARc/tree/c1d5ed407c9ee8ee0ae86a95b40069b15a586faf/bench-logs/2026-09-16-round2-recursion).

## Validation

Linux checks use Rust 1.95.0, strict warnings, eight Rayon workers and the repository test profile.

| Configuration | Native library tests | Core library tests |
|---|---:|---:|
| Default | 174 passed | 143 passed, 27 ignored |
| Serial | 176 passed | 117 passed, 20 ignored |
| Serial with ZK | 206 passed | Experimental dispatcher does not compile |

The library matrix was run at `d190e1419f5f1231818e69253cab5b7dda3d7165`; the serial tracer also passed 62 tests. The final head `b70711b0499dec29badc4d70152c2521b86ed91f` adds a shared commitment-length guard, a conditional backend import and equivalent serial iterator lint repairs in two files. The exact intervening diff is preserved in the validation record.

At the final head, formatting, serial core compilation, strict default workspace Clippy and strict optional-backend core Clippy pass. The serial affine native suite passes 176 tests. Three complete ordinary proofs, built with default parallel features, serial features, and serial plus `affine-msm,check-fixed-tables`, have identical canonical bytes, compact bytes and public inputs/outputs. Every build verifies both encodings, restores canonical bytes exactly, and rejects an altered output. The canonical SHA-256 is `5496c3b55a4618865fe01585fd103be18c29d02a10c78c25790f07c213015b38`.

The complete fixed-table reference test also passes at the final head, checking every embedded sine, cosine and sigmoid entry.

The experimental ONNX ZK dispatcher retains compilation failures. Its 41 primary strict-lint diagnostics match the exact prerequisite correctness head by message and source location. The serial ZK core test build retains the same 39 primary diagnostics as that prerequisite's core ZK test build. These failures are recorded separately from the passing native ZK suite. No complete workspace ZK test success or combined performance measurement is claimed.

# Add registered native BlindFold graph proofs and tensor boundaries

Separate hiding proofs do not by themselves establish that adjacent operations use the same hidden tensor or the verifier's registered public parameters. This change requires hiding openings and BlindFold constraints derived from the statement, shares original tensor commitments throughout a registered graph, refreshes private blinds and binds external tensor openings to an authenticated context.

**Topic** native foundations. **Type** New capability, binding checks and integration repairs. **Base** `review/tensor-correctness` ([#369](https://github.com/ICME-Lab/jolt-atlas/pull/369), review unit 1).

**Primary source PRs** [#316](https://github.com/ICME-Lab/jolt-atlas/pull/316), [#317](https://github.com/ICME-Lab/jolt-atlas/pull/317), [#318](https://github.com/ICME-Lab/jolt-atlas/pull/318), [#319](https://github.com/ICME-Lab/jolt-atlas/pull/319), [#329](https://github.com/ICME-Lab/jolt-atlas/pull/329), [#338](https://github.com/ICME-Lab/jolt-atlas/pull/338).

## Review order

1. Native hiding opening API and statement-derived constraints.
2. Lookup and multiplication primitives with mandatory integer ranges.
3. Shared graph commitments and grouped reduction.
4. Authenticated public parameter registration.
5. Original tensor boundary openings.

## Existing evidence

These are recorded comparisons for individual changes. Each has its own control and workload; performance of the combined branch is unmeasured. The original PRs retain source revisions, hardware, flags and artifact links.

| Scope | Recorded control | Recorded candidate | Change | Meaning and limits |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Four-table chain, 256 values, proving after commitments | 7.770 s | 2.042 s | 5.728 s lower (73.72%) | #319; one sample per configuration, includes required equality arguments in the separate-proof control |
| Same component proof size | 117.2 KiB | 31.5 KiB | About 85.7 KiB smaller (73.1%) | #319; small component, not a complete model projection |
| Different hidden producer or registered weights | Individually valid unrelated proof | Rejected by registered graph/boundary checks | Binding check | Binding regression; new capability, not an unsupported-old-API speed comparison |

## Implementation and review examples

This foundation supports registered vector graphs with multiplication and public table lookup. It authenticates public parameter commitments and the setup, keeps fresh private blinds, and opens the original tensor commitment at an external boundary bound to its context. Unsupported graph forms reject. Tensor shapes and scalar boundary fixtures arrive in the next PR, together with their required operators.

A useful negative example is a valid multiplication proof made with a different registered weight. The proof may verify against its own registration, but must fail against the recipient's expected registration. Likewise, independently valid proofs over different hidden producers do not satisfy the required boundary. This is a new capability and binding contract, not a claim that the earlier API supported private ONNX execution.

## Measurement conditions

The four-table comparison uses one observation per configuration on a Xeon E5-2699 v3, eight workers, Rust 1.97.1 and the optimized test profile. Proving excludes setup, witness construction and commitments. Proof size excludes the public statement and verifier data. Both configurations prove the same chain and include all required hidden equalities. Sources are pinned by the original application checkpoint `0f9eecc`; [the comparison and complete scope](https://github.com/ICME-Lab/zkARc/blob/cc299bc/native-atlas/graphs.md) retain the source manifest and all six fixtures.

Peak memory covers each complete proving process, including setup and its initial verification. At 256 values it falls from 22.5 to 15.3 MiB, while at eight values it rises from 9.0 to 10.2 MiB. These small single observations establish neither repeatability nor a complete model result.

## Validation

Linux validation at `0a7de79f`, Rust 1.95.0, strict warnings, eight Rayon workers and the repository test profile:

- Formatting passes. Native library tests pass 162 ordinary cases and 213 ZK cases.
- `cargo clippy -p joltworks --all-targets --features zk` passes.
- Strict Clippy for the whole workspace passes with and without `jolt-atlas-core/zk`. This includes the test and example targets.
- Registration, boundary, missing-opening and altered-statement rejection tests pass.

Unused experimental ONNX cache helpers and avoidable test input copies are cleaned up in separate commits. Compilation does not establish a complete private ONNX dispatcher; the new supported API is the native graph/component API. Combined-branch performance remains unmeasured.

## Experimental ONNX status

The separate `cargo test -p jolt-atlas-core --lib --features zk` run reports **127 passed, 26 failed and 29 ignored** at this head. Failures include unimplemented fused rescaling, clamped activations, sine/cosine and softmax, missing verifier relations, and failed division/gather verification. The two historical attack regressions also cannot complete through this dispatcher. Its unchanged base cannot compile with ZK, so these runtime failures are not described as an exact-base inherited-test result.

No test is disabled or changed to accept these failures. This PR supports the native graph/component API and does not complete the experimental ONNX dispatcher tracked in #289. Strict workspace Clippy passes, but the complete workspace ZK test job is not green.

# Prove exact native tensor arithmetic and layouts

Tensor arithmetic must match integer rescaling, clamping, padding and floor-division semantics, not just a field equation. This change adds clamped add/subtract, sums and means, contractions, reciprocal square root, softmax, broadcasts, layouts, slices and concatenation with the original hidden commitments.

**Topic** native operators. **Type** New relations and integer-semantics corrections. **Base** `review/native-foundations` ([#371](https://github.com/ICME-Lab/jolt-atlas/pull/371), review unit 3).

**Primary source PRs** [#320](https://github.com/ICME-Lab/jolt-atlas/pull/320), [#321](https://github.com/ICME-Lab/jolt-atlas/pull/321), [#322](https://github.com/ICME-Lab/jolt-atlas/pull/322), [#323](https://github.com/ICME-Lab/jolt-atlas/pull/323), [#324](https://github.com/ICME-Lab/jolt-atlas/pull/324), [#325](https://github.com/ICME-Lab/jolt-atlas/pull/325), [#326](https://github.com/ICME-Lab/jolt-atlas/pull/326), [#327](https://github.com/ICME-Lab/jolt-atlas/pull/327), [#328](https://github.com/ICME-Lab/jolt-atlas/pull/328).

## Review order

1. Clamped arithmetic and integer ranges.
2. Reductions and logical mean divisors.
3. Contractions and bounded operands.
4. Reciprocal square root and exact softmax.
5. Layouts, slices and concatenation.

## Existing evidence

These are recorded comparisons for individual changes. Each has its own control and workload; performance of the combined branch is unmeasured. The original PRs retain source revisions, hardware, flags and artifact links.

| Scope | Recorded control | Recorded candidate | Meaning and limits |
|---|---|---|---|
| Mean over 896 logical values stored in width 1,024 | Divisor derived from padded width | Divisor derived from the registered logical count | #328 correctness regression; no speedup claimed |
| Integer quotient illustration | 7 = 3 × 1 + 4 satisfies only the field equality | Require 0 ≤ remainder < 3, rejecting quotient 1 | Explain required constraints; this illustration is not a freshly executed forged-proof attack |

## Implementation and review examples

Review the integer constraints separately from the generic opening repair. An equation such as `7 = 3*1 + 4` does not prove quotient 1 when dividing by 3. The remainder must also be less than 3. Logical means use the registered count, so 896 meaningful values padded to 1,024 still divide by 896.

The generic opening repair handles public slice coordinates equal to zero. The shortcut previously divided by a vanishing equality factor when recovering a round endpoint. The repaired path computes that endpoint directly and checks the resulting polynomial against independent evaluation for both binding orders, Boolean coordinates and zero scale. This is a prover correctness repair; no forged-proof acceptance is asserted.

This extension gives graph edges their tensor shapes, restores the registered normalization example, and exercises scalar tensor boundaries. Rejection of uncommitted witnesses accompanies the constructor added in the following PR. It retains the public registration and boundary APIs from the foundation.

## Validation

Linux validation at `fb1b116c00b97e0a6855bb8517e4f93b33561bb4`, Rust 1.95.0, strict warnings, eight Rayon workers and the repository test profile:

- Formatting passes. Native library tests pass 163 ordinary cases and 259 ZK cases.
- Strict Clippy passes for every native library/example/test target with ZK and for the whole workspace with and without ZK.
- Tests compare the actual Atlas integer kernels, logical and padded sizes, scalar and Boolean points, false quotient/remainder/clamp witnesses and hidden producer substitutions.

Small fixture type/format repairs are separate commits. All proof predicates remain enforced. Performance of the combined branch remains unmeasured.

## Experimental ONNX scope

The foundation's separate ONNX ZK test run reports 127 passes, 26 failures and 29 ignored tests. That parent result is preserved in the validation record. This branch validates the native API and does not claim completion of the experimental ONNX dispatcher or a green complete-workspace ZK test job. No test or proof predicate is relaxed.

# Prove committed table access and greedy generation

Generation requires access to the original committed tables, exact selection rules, a first-maximum tie rule and a registered stopping condition. This change proves original-table access, integer division, masks and selection, then shifted greedy token choice and stopping over the original hidden tensors.

**Topic** native generation. **Type** New relations, witness hardening and a measured gather optimization. **Base** `review/native-operators` ([#372](https://github.com/ICME-Lab/jolt-atlas/pull/372), review unit 4).

**Primary source PRs** [#330](https://github.com/ICME-Lab/jolt-atlas/pull/330), [#331](https://github.com/ICME-Lab/jolt-atlas/pull/331), [#332](https://github.com/ICME-Lab/jolt-atlas/pull/332), [#333](https://github.com/ICME-Lab/jolt-atlas/pull/333), [#334](https://github.com/ICME-Lab/jolt-atlas/pull/334), [#336](https://github.com/ICME-Lab/jolt-atlas/pull/336), [#339](https://github.com/ICME-Lab/jolt-atlas/pull/339).

## Review order

1. Original committed tables and exact division.
2. Projected row gathers and isolated measurements.
3. Integer masks and checked witness construction.
4. First maximum over logical prefixes.
5. Shifted token selection, end tokens and stopping.

## Existing evidence

These are recorded comparisons for individual changes. Each has its own control and workload; performance of the combined branch is unmeasured. The original PRs retain source revisions, hardware, flags and artifact links.

| Scope | Recorded control | Recorded candidate | Change | Meaning and limits |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Gather fixture, complete proof plus statement | 102.1 KiB | 66.5 KiB | About 35.6 KiB smaller (34.9%) | #332; 8 indices, 1,024 columns, 256 rows; not a full embedding/model result |
| Same gather fixture, process peak including setup and both invocations | 506.7 MiB | 462.4 MiB | About 44.3 MiB lower (8.7%) | #332; two invocations per configuration |
| Equal maximum scores at indices 0 and 1 | Either index maximizes the score | Only index 0 satisfies the first-tie rule | Selection rule | #336 review example; also test logical vocabulary bounds and padding |

## Implementation and review examples

Table access binds to the original committed table, including after row projection. The selection relation enforces the first maximum within the logical vocabulary. If indices 0 and 1 have equal maximum scores, selecting 1 must fail. Response shifting, end tokens, stopping and padding are constrained separately.

Selection alone does not establish model provenance. The caller also requires the accepted causal model execution and canonical tensor conversion proofs for the same hidden values.

## Measurement conditions

The gather comparison uses the same hidden values on a Xeon E5-2699 v3 with eight workers. Each configuration has two invocations sharing one setup, with alternating configuration order. Proving excludes witness construction and commitments; process peak includes setup, registration, both proofs and their initial verification. Proof size includes the statement. [Pinned measurements and source evidence](https://github.com/ICME-Lab/zkARc/blob/cc299bc/native-atlas/row-gathers.md).

## Validation

Linux validation at `02163ea6302999fc84fb49468c4a064ad3f4466d`, Rust 1.95.0, strict warnings, eight Rayon workers and the repository test profile:

- Formatting and `cargo clippy -p joltworks --all-targets --features zk` pass.
- Native library tests pass 163 ordinary cases and 295 ZK cases.
- Controls cover false integer witnesses, changed commitments and producers, invalid indices, later tied maxima, wrong response tokens, stopping and padding. The uncommitted-witness boundary control is included with the constructor it exercises.

This validates the native relations. Selection still requires the accepted causal model execution and conversion proofs described above. Performance of the combined branch remains unmeasured.

## Experimental ONNX scope

The foundation's separate ONNX ZK test run reports 127 passes, 26 failures and 29 ignored tests. That parent result is preserved in the validation record. This branch validates the native API and does not claim completion of the experimental ONNX dispatcher or a green complete-workspace ZK test job. No test or proof predicate is relaxed.

## Source identity

| Original PR | Head reviewed |
